articles.title: Install Ultimate Macro
articles.summary: From ZIP download to first launch.

sections.title: Download and extract
steps: Download the ZIP from the official Ultimate Macro download page.
Right-click the ZIP and extract the whole archive to a folder. Do not run Main.ahk inside the ZIP.
Install 64-bit AutoHotkey v2 from autohotkey.com/v2. AutoHotkey v1.1 will not work.
Open Main.ahk in the extracted folder.

sections.title: Before your first run
checks: Windows resolution: supported 16:9; scaling: 100% recommended
Windows taskbar: visible
Roblox: 60 FPS, Classic camera, Manual graphics
TDS: Large UI, Screen Shake off, Vertical Upgrades on

articles.title: Requirements
articles.summary: Supported Windows versions, resolution and dependencies.

sections.title: Recommended
paragraphs: 1920×1080 at 100% Windows scaling is the easiest baseline for troubleshooting. Other supported 16:9 resolutions are supported by the documented adaptive detection path.
A slower PC may need longer mouse, key or upgrade delays.

articles.title: Run your first strategy
articles.summary: Test a built-in strategy before leaving the macro unattended.

sections.title: Start a test run
steps: Open Roblox and join Tower Defense Simulator.
Open Ultimate Macro. On the Main tab, select a strategy that came with the release.
Confirm you have the towers required by that strategy.
Make sure Windows, Roblox, and TDS settings match the setup pages.
Select Start or press F1.
Watch a full match, including upgrades and the end-of-match screen.

sections.title: Stop safely
paragraphs: Press F2 to stop the macro and release held input. Check placement, upgrades, result detection, and the next-match transition before running longer sessions.

articles.title: Windows display & OCR
articles.summary: Configure the screen settings used by image detection.

sections.title: Check before running
steps: Open Windows Settings → System → Display and confirm resolution and scale.
Make the taskbar visible in Windows taskbar settings.
Ensure the English (US) OCR language pack is available.
Do not move or resize Roblox while a run is in progress.

sections.title: When clicks miss
paragraphs: If the macro clicks the wrong location, check display geometry before increasing delays. The macro uses screen coordinates and image matching.

articles.title: Roblox settings
articles.summary: Use the game settings expected by the documented macro.

sections.title: Avoid layout changes
paragraphs: Do not use custom Roblox fonts. They can cause wave and currency OCR to read text incorrectly. Keep the game window at the same size and location during a session.

articles.title: TDS settings
articles.summary: Match the interface layout expected by tower placement and upgrades.

articles.title: Hotkeys & keybinds
articles.summary: Playback and recording shortcuts in the documented release.

sections.title: Change shortcuts
paragraphs: Recording shortcuts are configurable under Settings → Recording Hotkeys. For abilities, confirm the keybinds in Settings → TDS Keybinds also match TDS.

articles.title: Record a strategy
articles.summary: Turn a played match into a .strat file.

sections.title: Before recording
paragraphs: Pick your map, mode and tower loadout. Confirm the game and recording keybinds first. The recorder captures actions as you play, not a guaranteed successful strategy.

sections.title: Record and save
steps: Open Create → Record a Strategy.
Play a match normally. Use the recording shortcuts for placement, upgrades, selling and other actions.
If an action was recorded incorrectly, use Delete Record (Ctrl + B) before continuing.
Finish recording and save the result as a .strat file.
Replay the new strategy under supervision before sharing it.

sections.title: Recording tip
paragraphs: Leave enough time for game animations and currency changes. Fast manual actions may need longer delays to replay reliably on other PCs.

articles.title: Edit a strategy
articles.summary: Open a .strat file in Strategy Lab.

sections.title: Open Strategy Lab
steps: In Ultimate Macro, open Create.
Choose Edit a Strategy or Open Strategy Lab.
Open the .strat file you want to inspect or change.
Save a separate copy before replacing a strategy that already works.

sections.title: Standalone editor
paragraphs: You can also launch StrategyLab.exe from the release folder. Strategy Lab is the visual editor for strategy actions. Test an edited strategy before relying on it.

articles.title: Rotate strategies
articles.summary: Alternate between two strategies after a run count or time limit.

sections.title: Configure rotation
steps: On the Main tab, choose the two strategies you want to alternate.
Enable Strategy Rotation.
Set Swap after to a number of Runs or Minutes.
Test each strategy on its own before starting rotation.

sections.title: Check compatibility
paragraphs: The selected strategies may require different maps or towers. Make sure both can run with your current loadout and settings.

articles.title: Find community strategies
articles.summary: Browse and test shared .strat files in Strategy Network.

sections.title: Use a shared strategy
steps: Open Strategy Network and find a strategy for your mode or map.
Check the tower loadout and other listed requirements.
Download or choose the strategy through the supported workflow.
Run a supervised match before leaving it unattended.

sections.title: After a game update
paragraphs: An older strategy may no longer match current game behavior, even if its file loads. Check its requirements and look for a newer version if it fails.

articles.title: Long session settings
articles.summary: Goals, timescale, and between-match actions.

sections.title: Goals and Timescale
rows: Set a currency target; the macro selects compatible strategies until the goal is reached.
In Settings, use 1.5× or 2× with available timescale tickets.

sections.title: Between matches
rows: Used after a loss; enabled by default.
Used after a win; enabled by default.
Verifies the destination map after joining and reloads if wrong. Recommended on.
Claims playtime and daily rewards when available.

sections.title: Before a long session
paragraphs: Watch one full match first. If you are running a win-only strategy and Restart lands you on the wrong map, try disabling the restart action.

articles.title: Party & VIP servers
articles.summary: Private server links and Host/Member party configuration.

sections.title: VIP server
steps: Paste a private server link into VIP Server Link.
Enable Use VIP Server.
Confirm that the Roblox account can join that server manually before testing the macro.

sections.title: Party mode
steps: Open the Party tab.
Select Host to create a party and invite others, or Member to wait for an invite.
Enter the host's display name and members' names.
Choose whether to return to the lobby when all or any party member leaves.
Save and test the group with all accounts present.

articles.title: Back up your setup
articles.summary: Export or import settings, hotkeys and strategies with Profile Manager.

sections.title: Export before changing your setup
paragraphs: Profile Manager bundles settings, hotkeys and strategies for backup or moving to another PC. Export a working configuration before experimenting.

sections.title: Import with care
paragraphs: Check the import preview before replacing existing settings, hotkeys or strategies.

articles.title: Built-in tools
articles.summary: Auto Call of Arms, Auto Spin, and Auto Open Consumable.

sections.title: Open a tool
paragraphs: The Tools tab opens utilities in separate always-on-top windows. F3 starts the selected tool; F4 stops it.

sections.title: Available tools
rows: Triggers Call of Arms and Drop the Beat on configured intervals; each ability can be disabled.
Claims spinning-wheel prizes and counts tickets used.
Opens consumable crates and counts how many were opened.

articles.title: Main.ahk won't open
articles.summary: Fix common startup failures.

sections.title: Check in this order
steps: Extract the entire ZIP before running anything.
Install 64-bit AutoHotkey v2.0. v1.1 cannot run Main.ahk.
Make sure .ahk files open using the AutoHotkey v2 launcher.
Close Roblox Account Manager and other multi-instance utilities.
Open Main.ahk again.

sections.title: If the error remains
paragraphs: Share the exact error, AutoHotkey version and Ultimate Macro version when requesting support.

articles.title: Clicks miss or towers won't place
articles.summary: Check display geometry before changing timing.

sections.title: Fix screen-related misses
steps: Check Windows resolution is supported 16:9 and scaling is preferably 100%.
Keep the Windows taskbar visible.
Set TDS UI Scale to Large and turn Screen Shake off.
Focus Roblox. Avoid resizing or moving its window once the run starts.
Test a bundled strategy for one match.

sections.title: If actions are late rather than misplaced
paragraphs: Try a higher Mouse Delay or Key Delay in Settings. A timing issue is different from a consistent wrong click position.

articles.title: Wave or cash detection is wrong
articles.summary: Correct missing OCR language support and font changes.

sections.title: Fix OCR
steps: Install the English (United States) Windows OCR language pack.
Remove custom Roblox font modifications.
Use 100% Windows scaling as a test baseline.
Keep wave and currency UI visible and unobstructed.
Run a short test and compare the on-screen value to the value in macro logs.

sections.title: Still incorrect?
paragraphs: Save the release version, screen resolution and a cropped screenshot showing the wrong value. Remove private details before sharing it.

articles.title: Upgrades fail or use the wrong path
articles.summary: Check the upgrade panel, money, keybinds and delay.

sections.title: Troubleshoot upgrades
steps: Confirm the tower has enough cash for the action.
Enable Prefer Vertical Upgrades in TDS.
Check that the upgrade and bottom-path keybinds in Ultimate Macro match your game settings.
Increase Upgrade Delay in Settings if the panel opens slowly.
Replay the same step while supervising and record which upgrade was missed.

sections.title: What changes the diagnosis
paragraphs: If the macro clicked the wrong button, check UI settings. If it clicked before the panel appeared, increase the delay. These are different problems.

articles.title: Abilities don't activate
articles.summary: Fix mismatched TDS ability keybinds.

sections.title: Check both sets of keybinds
steps: Open TDS and find the key assigned to the ability.
Open Ultimate Macro → Settings → TDS Keybinds.
Set the matching key in both places.
Test the ability manually, then in a short supervised macro run.

sections.title: Why there may be no error
paragraphs: The macro sends the configured key press. If the game expects a different key, no action happens, even though the macro sent its input.

articles.title: Auto Equip or targeting stopped working
articles.summary: Legacy Mode deliberately disables some features.

sections.title: Check Legacy Mode
paragraphs: Legacy Mode disables Auto Equip and target changes. Turn it off to use those features.

sections.title: What to do
steps: Open Settings and check whether Legacy Mode is enabled.
Disable it to use the adaptive image-detection path.
Retest Auto Equip and tower targeting.
Only use Legacy Mode as a fallback when necessary; it can retain 1920×1080 limitations.

articles.title: Stuck after a match
articles.summary: Check restart, play-again, and map verification.

sections.title: Check the transition
steps: Check whether the macro stopped on a win, loss, lobby, or Ready screen.
Verify that Click Restart and Click Play Again are configured for your strategy.
Keep Check the map enabled so a wrong map can be detected.
Stop with F2 and replay a single strategy while watching the transition.
Save the last log entry and the screen state if it gets stuck again.

sections.title: Wrong map after a win-only run?
paragraphs: Disable Click Restart if a win-only strategy sends you to the wrong map.

articles.title: Roblox disconnects during a run
articles.summary: What recovery handles and what to check when it stalls.

sections.title: Automatic recovery
paragraphs: Ultimate Macro can reconnect Roblox and re-enter TDS after a disconnect. If it stops at a login prompt or unexpected dialog, use the checks below.

sections.title: If it doesn't rejoin
steps: Check whether Roblox can connect normally.
Dismiss unexpected Roblox dialogs or login prompts.
Stop with F2 if possible and save the recent logs.
Retry while watching the reconnect sequence and identify the screen where it gets stuck.

articles.title: Discord updates aren't arriving
articles.summary: Separate webhook failures from remote-control failures.

sections.title: Webhook test
steps: Open the macro's Discord tab.
Use Test Webhook with your configured URL.
If it fails, confirm the webhook still exists and the right URL was pasted.
Check whether Discord message permissions or channel settings have changed.

sections.title: Remote commands
paragraphs: Check that the macro runs locally, then try a bot status request. If that fails, verify the connection for your version.

sections.title: Keep secrets private
paragraphs: Never paste webhook URLs or bot tokens into public support posts. Rotate a URL or token if it leaks.

articles.title: Send logs to Discord
articles.summary: Set up a webhook for run logs, stats and screenshots.

sections.title: Create a private webhook
steps: In a Discord server, open a channel's settings → Integrations → Webhooks.
Create a webhook and copy its URL.
Open the macro's Discord tab, paste the URL and enable the webhook.
Select the information you want to send, then use Test Webhook.

sections.title: Available reports
rows: Currency and session numbers read with OCR.
Local debug events forwarded to Discord.
Result-screen images, optionally sent to a second webhook.

sections.title: Privacy
paragraphs: Treat a webhook URL as a password. Screenshots may show account names or other on-screen details.

articles.title: Remote control from Discord
articles.summary: Use documented EngineerBot or personal-bot commands.

sections.title: What it can do
checks: Start and stop the macro
Request status or a screenshot
Check version, stats and logs
Check or select the strategy (where supported)

sections.title: Before enabling
paragraphs: Test a status command before relying on remote controls. Available commands depend on the installed version; keep bot credentials private.

articles.title: Discord community
articles.summary: Find announcements, strategies and support.

sections.title: Official server
paragraphs: The official Discord hosts announcements, community strategies and support. See the current channels for roles and events.

sections.title: Before asking for help
checks: Macro version
What you were doing
What happened versus what you expected
Relevant log or screenshot with personal details removed

articles.title: Report an issue
articles.summary: Give developers a reproducible report instead of a vague description.

sections.title: Collect the important details
steps: Enable Debug Logs in Settings.
Reproduce the problem once, if safe.
Note the version, Windows resolution and game settings.
Describe the expected result and actual result.
Attach the relevant log and a redacted screenshot when useful.
Search existing GitHub issues before filing a new one.

sections.title: Where to send it
paragraphs: Send the report to GitHub Issues or the official Discord support channel. Remove credentials and webhook URLs from any logs.

articles.title: About Ultimate Macro
articles.summary: Project background and license.

sections.title: What it is
paragraphs: Ultimate Macro is a free, open-source Windows macro for Roblox Tower Defense Simulator. It uses image detection and OCR rather than injecting code into Roblox.

sections.title: Open source
paragraphs: The New Era continues the project originally created by Darksen. The public code is distributed under GPL-3.0. Read the repository for license terms, contributors and releases.

sections.title: Not an official Roblox product
paragraphs: Ultimate Macro is a third-party tool and is not affiliated with Roblox or Paradoxum Games. Automation carries account and game-policy risks.

articles.title: Macro is slow or misses inputs
articles.summary: Adjust timing and performance settings without breaking placement.

sections.title: Change one delay at a time
steps: Open Ultimate Macro Settings.
If upgrades are skipped while the upgrade panel loads, raise Upgrade Delay.
If mouse actions happen too quickly, increase Mouse Delay.
If key presses are missed, increase Key Delay.
Test a short run after each adjustment so you know which change helped.

sections.title: On weaker PCs
paragraphs: Potato Mode lowers macro overhead on slower machines. Try it before switching image detection methods.
checks: Keep Legacy Mode off unless needed as a fallback.
Legacy Mode may be limited to 1920×1080 and disables Auto Equip and target changes.

articles.title: Record DJ and tower abilities
articles.summary: Hotkeys for DJ tracks, Necromancer and Brawler actions.

sections.title: DJ track changes
paragraphs: The existing recorder also supports scheduling DJ disc changes by wave.
steps: Open Create → Record a Strategy.
During the match, use Ctrl + D to record a DJ track change.
Save the .strat file and replay it to confirm the track change is timed correctly.

sections.title: Necromancer and Brawler
paragraphs: To record Raise the Dead (Necromancer) or a Brawler reposition, hold Ctrl with the ability's in-game keybind. These actions do not use a separate recording shortcut.
checks: Confirm the ability keybinds in Ultimate Macro match TDS.
Test the strategy before sharing it.

articles.title: Use Timescale tickets
articles.summary: Configure 1.5× or 2× matches when you have tickets.

sections.title: Configure Timescale
steps: Confirm that timescale tickets are available on the Roblox account.
Open Ultimate Macro Settings.
Set Timescale to 1.5× or 2×.
Run one match while watching its timing and game transitions.

sections.title: Check the strategy
paragraphs: Faster games reduce run time, but a strategy still needs to work at the selected speed. Return to standard speed if the run repeatedly stalls or misses actions.

articles.title: Use official release downloads
articles.summary: Find trusted ZIP files and check which release you are installing.

sections.title: Where to download
paragraphs: Use the Ultimate Macro download page or the releases published by UltimateMacro/Ultimate-Macro-New-Era. The source repository itself is not a substitute for the complete packaged ZIP.
steps: Open the Download page or official GitHub Releases.
Choose the release you want to use and read its notes.
Download its ZIP asset, then extract it completely.

sections.title: Before updating
paragraphs: Keep a copy of your working custom .strat files and configuration. Test any version change with a short supervised run.

articles.title: Keep release folders together
articles.summary: Why Main.ahk must stay beside its libraries and resources.

sections.title: Required layout
paragraphs: Extract the release as a complete folder. Main.ahk relies on companion files and folders such as lib, Resources and submacros.
steps: Extract all ZIP contents, not only Main.ahk.
Keep the original directory structure.
Launch Main.ahk from inside that extracted folder.

sections.title: When files go missing
paragraphs: Download the official release again, extract it into a clean folder, and compare folder contents before transferring personal strategies.

articles.title: AutoHotkey v1 vs v2
articles.summary: Make sure Main.ahk uses the 64-bit v2 interpreter.

sections.title: Check the association
paragraphs: Both AutoHotkey versions can coexist on Windows.
steps: Install 64-bit AutoHotkey v2.
Check the default application for .ahk files.
Open Main.ahk again with the v2 launcher.
If a 32-bit warning appears, change to the 64-bit build.

articles.title: First-match checklist
articles.summary: Use one match to confirm the whole playback loop.

sections.title: Before pressing F1
checks: Supported 16:9 resolution and visible Windows taskbar
TDS UI Scale: Large, Screen Shake: Disabled
Roblox at 60 FPS with Classic camera
Correct tower loadout and TDS keybinds

sections.title: During the run
steps: Watch the first placement and confirm the tower appears.
Confirm at least one upgrade follows the intended path.
Watch for end-of-match detection and correct return to the next game.
Stop with F2 if anything mismatches and note which step failed.

articles.title: Auto Equip Towers
articles.summary: Let a strategy's required towers be equipped before the match.

sections.title: Enable it
paragraphs: The Main tab offers Auto Equip Towers for strategies with a defined loadout.
steps: Choose a strategy with tower requirements.
Confirm the Roblox account owns every required tower, including golden variants.
Enable Auto Equip Towers.
Observe the loadout before your first match.

sections.title: Limits
paragraphs: Auto Equip cannot equip a tower the account doesn't own. It is unavailable in Legacy Mode.

articles.title: Default TDS ability keybinds
articles.summary: Match the recorded macro keys to Tower Defense Simulator.

sections.title: Verify both sides
paragraphs: In Ultimate Macro open Settings → TDS Keybinds, then compare each assigned key with TDS itself. A mismatch can make an ability do nothing without an error.

articles.title: Community and My Strats
articles.summary: Use the Main tab's built-in strategy browser.

sections.title: Choose a source
paragraphs: On Main → Strategies, Community contains shared strategy cards and My Strats contains your own files.
steps: Open the Strategies browser.
Use Community to inspect a shared strategy, or My Strats for your recordings.
Use Browse to select a local .strat file when needed.
Review required towers, map and mode before pressing Start.

sections.title: Don't skip the test
paragraphs: Community cards and download metadata do not guarantee a strategy will work after a TDS update. Watch its first match.

articles.title: Strategy recording setup
articles.summary: Set map, mode, towers and modifiers before capturing actions.

sections.title: Create → Record a Strategy
steps: Choose the map and mode from the dropdowns.
Enter required towers as a comma-separated list.
For a golden tower, prefix the name with G, for example G Minigunner.
Hold Ctrl while selecting multiple modifiers.
Choose ability toggles, wave skipping and optional starting movement as needed.
Record your match and save its .strat file.

sections.title: Supported mode families
paragraphs: The documented recorder includes Easy, Casual, Intermediate, Molten, Fallen, Frost, Hardcore, Voidcore and Arcade, plus map-specific selections. The game may change available modes.

articles.title: Record multiple modifiers
articles.summary: Use Ctrl selection when preparing a strategy recording.

sections.title: Choose modifiers
steps: Open Create → Record a Strategy.
Find the Modifiers control.
Hold Ctrl while selecting or deselecting additional modifiers.
Confirm your selection before starting the match.
Save and replay the strategy to verify the configuration.

sections.title: Why record metadata
paragraphs: A strategy without correct mode and modifier information can run on the wrong configuration even when its actions are valid.

articles.title: Specify golden tower requirements
articles.summary: How the recording loadout denotes golden variants.

sections.title: Tower list format
paragraphs: Recording accepts a comma-separated tower list. Use the G prefix for a golden version, such as G Minigunner, alongside regular names like Ranger or Commander.

sections.title: Check before sharing
steps: Confirm the golden tower variant is required by the strategy.
Include it in the recording metadata.
Tell users they must own it before trying Auto Equip.
Test that the matching loadout is equipped.

articles.title: Recording ability options
articles.summary: Understand the recording controls for abilities and wave skipping.

sections.title: Available recording options
rows: Record or enable relevant ability automation
Set the recorder's repeated ability option

sections.title: Before replay
paragraphs: Confirm game keybinds and ability ownership on the receiving account. A toggle is not proof a tower or ability is available.

articles.title: Record opening movement
articles.summary: Configure optional starting movement before tower placement.

sections.title: Move option
paragraphs: The documented recording form can move your Roblox character in a chosen direction for a specified number of milliseconds at the start of a run.

sections.title: Use carefully
steps: Open the recording setup.
Choose a starting direction only when the strategy requires it.
Set a short movement duration in milliseconds.
Record and test the opening sequence before extending the duration.

articles.title: Record a repeatable strategy
articles.summary: Avoid capturing rushed actions that fail on replay.

sections.title: Before recording
paragraphs: The recorder saves what you actually do. A winning match doesn't guarantee a repeatable strategy if clicks and upgrades are too tightly spaced.

sections.title: Improve your recording
steps: Use stable Windows and TDS settings.
Allow UI panels to open before taking the next action.
Wait for cash to become available before upgrading.
Use descriptive filenames, for example pw2_solo_farm.strat.
Replay the finished file and watch the whole match.

articles.title: Record split upgrade paths
articles.summary: Capture the intended top or bottom upgrade path.

sections.title: Record upgrades
paragraphs: The recorded strategy format supports top and bottom upgrade paths as separate actions.
steps: Confirm TDS Prefer Vertical Upgrades is enabled.
Record the tower placement first.
Use the correct upgrade hotkey for the intended path.
Save the .strat and replay until you confirm the right path was upgraded.

sections.title: Troubleshoot
paragraphs: If paths differ during replay, verify TDS keybinds and panel layout. Increase Upgrade Delay only when the panel is late opening.

articles.title: Undo the last recorded action
articles.summary: Remove a mistaken recorder action with Ctrl + B.

sections.title: During recording
steps: Pause before recording the next action.
Press Ctrl + B to remove the last recorded action.
Check the remaining sequence before continuing.
Save a separate test .strat and replay it to verify the correction.

sections.title: Default hotkey
paragraphs: Ctrl + B is the documented default Delete Record shortcut; it can be changed in Recording Hotkeys.

articles.title: Schedule DJ discs by wave
articles.summary: Use wave-based DJ track changes instead of manual timing where supported.

sections.title: Available recording behavior
paragraphs: The documented recorder supports DJ disc changes with Ctrl + D and a wave-based schedule.

sections.title: Validate the sequence
steps: Set the intended DJ change in the strategy's recording flow.
Confirm the starting DJ track.
Run a supervised replay and note the wave on which the disc actually changes.
Adjust the strategy if the match reaches the change earlier than expected.

articles.title: Rotate strategies after runs
articles.summary: Switch between two strategies after a chosen run count.

sections.title: Main tab
steps: Select two strategies on Main.
Enable Strategy Rotation.
Choose Runs for Swap after.
Enter how many runs to complete before switching.
Watch at least one switch to confirm both strategies start correctly.

sections.title: Pre-check
paragraphs: Both strategies need compatible maps, modes and tower loadouts.

articles.title: Rotate strategies after minutes
articles.summary: Use a time interval rather than a run count.

sections.title: Main tab
steps: Choose two strategies.
Turn on Strategy Rotation.
Choose Minutes under Swap after.
Set the intended interval.
Watch the first switch and verify the target strategy.

sections.title: Avoid surprises
paragraphs: The time setting controls rotation; it does not make an incompatible strategy work with the current towers.

articles.title: Set a currency goal
articles.summary: Let the macro select compatible strategies until a target is met.

sections.title: Goal behavior
paragraphs: The documented Goals feature uses a currency target, not only a fixed number of runs, and selects compatible strategies toward it.

sections.title: Set up
steps: Open the session goal controls in your installed version.
Choose the currency and target.
Check that compatible strategies are available.
Watch the first run and confirm progress updates.
Verify that the session stops at the intended target.

articles.title: Restart, Play Again and map checks
articles.summary: Set the behavior the macro uses between matches.

sections.title: Options
rows: Used after a loss; normally enabled
Used after a win; normally enabled
Verifies the destination map and can reload if incorrect
Claims available daily and playtime rewards

sections.title: Recommended test
paragraphs: Run one match and observe the result-screen action and map selection. For a win-only strategy entering the wrong map, try turning Restart off.

articles.title: Check Timescale ticket prompts
articles.summary: Diagnose a Timescale prompt before a faster run.

sections.title: First checks
steps: Confirm the account has the required Timescale tickets.
Select 1.5× or 2× in Settings.
Run once under supervision and watch the confirmation flow.
If a ticket prompt prevents starting, return to normal speed and collect the exact prompt.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: The documented public release supports Timescale. Confirm button labels and confirmation behavior against the installed build before escalating a bug.

articles.title: Start from lobby or Ready screen
articles.summary: How resume-aware startup handles a running Roblox session.

sections.title: Supported states
paragraphs: Documented releases can start while Roblox is already in the TDS lobby or on the Ready screen.

sections.title: Before testing
steps: Check the correct Roblox window is focused.
Open the macro with a known-good strategy.
Observe the existing game state being recognized.
Stop with F2 if it attempts a wrong transition.

articles.title: Pre-run diagnostics
articles.summary: Review resolution, scaling, OCR and dependencies before playing.

sections.title: What is checked
paragraphs: The documented pre-run diagnostics include Windows resolution, display scaling, OCR and missing dependencies.

sections.title: If a check fails
steps: Identify the failing prerequisite.
Open the matching Windows or macro setting.
Correct it without changing unrelated settings.
Rerun the check before starting a long session.

articles.title: Discord session statistics
articles.summary: Understand OCR-based session information sent to Discord.

sections.title: Enable the report
steps: Create a private Discord webhook.
Enable the webhook from the macro's Discord tab.
Select Send Statistics.
Use Test Webhook, then check a live match update.

sections.title: What numbers mean
paragraphs: Statistics are read with OCR. If a value is wrong, fix Windows OCR and Roblox fonts before treating it as a Discord problem.

articles.title: Discord screenshot notifications
articles.summary: Use periodic and result-screen screenshots to follow a run.

sections.title: Available images
paragraphs: Automatic screenshots can be sent periodically; Triumph and Loss screenshots capture the end-of-match result screen. The result images can use a second webhook.

sections.title: Privacy check
steps: Choose a private channel.
Enable the screenshot types you want.
Check a test result for user names or other personal details.
Share only redacted examples with public support.

articles.title: Keep Discord webhook URLs private
articles.summary: A leaked webhook can be used to post into your channel.

sections.title: Before sharing configuration
steps: Do not paste a webhook URL into a public issue or Discord message.
Redact the URL from screenshots and logs.
Use a private channel for the macro's screenshots and session events.
If leaked, delete or regenerate the webhook in Discord and update the macro settings.

articles.title: EngineerBot remote commands
articles.summary: Supported remote start, stop, screenshot and status controls.

sections.title: Supported actions
rows: Inspect what the Windows PC shows

sections.title: Before trusting remote stop
paragraphs: Test local F2 control first and verify the bot's connection. Discord connectivity cannot repair a broken local macro session.

articles.title: Export a working profile
articles.summary: Back up settings, hotkeys and strategies in one bundle.

sections.title: Before changing versions
steps: Open Profile Manager.
Export the working settings, hotkeys and strategies.
Save the file somewhere outside the release folder.
Check the backup exists before editing or importing another setup.

articles.title: Import a profile safely
articles.summary: Restore a bundle without losing your current setup.

sections.title: Protect the existing profile
steps: Export your current working profile first.
Open Profile Manager and select Import.
Review its preview of settings, hotkeys and strategies.
Confirm the intended replacements and keep a backup.
Test one strategy after importing.

articles.title: Tools shortcuts: F3 and F4
articles.summary: Start and stop the separate tools from their own windows.

sections.title: Tool controls
paragraphs: The Tools tab opens utilities in always-on-top windows. F3 starts the selected tool and F4 stops it.
steps: Choose Auto Call of Arms, Auto Spin or Auto Open Consumable.
Open the tool's window.
Press F3 to begin its task.
Press F4 to stop it.

articles.title: Auto Call of Arms
articles.summary: Run supported abilities at configured intervals.

sections.title: Set up intervals
steps: Open Tools → Auto Call of Arms.
Choose the Call of Arms and Drop the Beat ability options.
Set each desired interval in seconds.
Make sure the Settings keybinds match TDS.
Press F3 to start and F4 to stop.

sections.title: Important
paragraphs: Either ability can be disabled independently. The tool cannot activate an unavailable in-game ability.

articles.title: Auto Spin
articles.summary: Automate the spinning wheel with the separate Auto Spin tool.

sections.title: Using Auto Spin
steps: Open Tools → Auto Spin.
Check the spin interface is available in TDS.
Press F3 to start the tool.
Monitor the ticket count while it runs.
Press F4 to stop.

sections.title: Counter
paragraphs: The documented tool counts how many tickets were used.

articles.title: Auto Open Consumable
articles.summary: Use the standalone crate-opening utility.

sections.title: Opening consumables
steps: Open Tools → Auto Open Consumable.
Confirm the intended consumables are available.
Press F3 to start opening crates.
Watch the count and stop with F4.

sections.title: Counter
paragraphs: The tool reports how many crates it opened.

articles.title: Legacy Mode and resolution limits
articles.summary: Why Legacy Mode is a fallback for display detection.

sections.title: Known limitation
paragraphs: The public setup guide warns that Legacy Mode can retain 1920×1080 limitations and disables Auto Equip and target changes. Use adaptive detection when possible.

sections.title: Test
steps: Check whether Legacy Mode is enabled.
Disable it if Auto Equip or target changes are needed.
Use a supported 16:9 resolution; test at 1920×1080 if troubleshooting.
Retest with a bundled strategy before returning to long runs.

articles.title: Install missing OCR language
articles.summary: Correct text detection when English (US) OCR support is absent.

sections.title: Windows requirement
paragraphs: Ultimate Macro uses Windows OCR for currency, wave numbers and result screens.
steps: Install the English (United States) Windows OCR language pack.
Reopen Ultimate Macro after installation.
Remove any custom Roblox fonts.
Compare a live wave/currency value against the macro's detection.

sections.title: When reporting
paragraphs: Include a cropped screenshot of the value being read incorrectly, the resolution, scaling and release version.

articles.title: Bottom-path upgrade key mismatch
articles.summary: Check the macro's upgrade and bottom path bindings.

sections.title: Check the keys
paragraphs: The setup guide lists E for Upgrade and Z for Bottom path as defaults.
steps: Open TDS and check its current upgrade and path shortcuts.
Open Ultimate Macro Settings → TDS Keybinds.
Make the matching keys identical.
Enable TDS Prefer Vertical Upgrades.
Replay one upgrade and verify the intended path.

articles.title: Capture debug logs for support
articles.summary: Record the event around a failure without sharing private data.

sections.title: Reproduce and collect
steps: Open Settings and enable Debug Logs.
Run until the failure happens once.
Note the last successful action and the action that should have followed.
Collect the relevant local log excerpt, with personal information removed.
Include macro version, Windows resolution and screen scaling in the support report.

sections.title: What makes a report useful
paragraphs: A short reproducible log is more useful than an entire unrelated session history.

articles.title: Open Strategy Lab
articles.summary: Launch the visual .strat editor from the Create tab or release folder.

sections.title: Two entry points
steps: Open Ultimate Macro and select Create → Open Strategy Lab or Edit a Strategy.
Alternatively, run StrategyLab.exe from the fully extracted release folder.
Open a copy of the .strat you want to inspect.

sections.title: Backup
paragraphs: Strategy Lab is a visual editor. Save a backup before changing the original strategy file.

articles.title: Version-specific release notes
articles.summary: Use release notes to understand changed behavior across builds.

sections.title: Find source-of-truth details
steps: Open the official GitHub Releases page.
Find the tag matching the installation you're using.
Read its new features, improvements and bug fixes.
Compare an observed behavior with the release it was introduced or fixed in.

sections.title: Avoid guessing
paragraphs: A feature described for one release may not exist in older versions. The current wiki baseline documents public v1.3.x behavior.

articles.title: Adaptive resolution support
articles.summary: Supported 16:9 display sizes and the recommended baseline.

sections.title: Supported displays
paragraphs: The public 1.3.5 release supports resolution-aware image detection from 720p through 4K, with 8K scaling included. The guide lists the supported 16:9 range from 1280×720 through 3840×2160.

sections.title: If actions miss
paragraphs: Confirm your resolution, scaling and Roblox window placement first. Increasing timing delays does not fix consistently wrong coordinates.

articles.title: Do I need an account?
articles.summary: Account requirements for the public v1.3.x local macro.

sections.title: Public v1.3.x behavior
paragraphs: The published setup guide states that Ultimate Macro runs locally and does not require an account.

sections.title: Check before a new version
paragraphs: Account behavior may change in later builds. Follow the release notes for the installed version rather than assuming this is permanent.

articles.title: Host a TDS party
articles.summary: Configure the Host role and invitation names.

sections.title: Host setup
steps: Open the Party tab and choose Host.
Enter the members' account names.
Choose when to return to the lobby, when all members or any member leaves.
Save the party configuration.
Test with the other accounts present before an unattended run.

articles.title: Join as a party member
articles.summary: Configure the Member role to wait for a host invitation.

sections.title: Member setup
steps: Open the Party tab and choose Member.
Enter the host's display name.
Choose the expected leave/rejoin behavior.
Save, then wait for the host invitation.
Verify all accounts entered the same match.

articles.title: Use a VIP server link
articles.summary: Configure a Roblox private server for macro runs.

sections.title: VIP server setup
steps: Check that the account has access to the intended server.
Copy the private server link.
Paste it into VIP Server Link.
Enable Use VIP Server.
Join and verify the correct experience before a long run.
